items.title: NEW — the `css` block's declarations become CALLS: `property: value;` → `property(value);`, the strategy element syntax took for attributes (`type("checkbox")`, `stroke-width("2")`), so `css { outline("none"); width(pct(100)); .script_label(); }` — the property keeps its hyphenated CSS name, its ARGUMENTS are ordinary vilan expressions (`pct(100)`, `Color::current().alpha(0.5)`, `size.get(4)` — no `{expr}` holes, no CSS token soup), and a dotted item without a block `.method(args);` is the method call on the chain (today a nested-rule head REQUIRES `{ … }`). The lowering does not move: every declaration is still exactly one `.raw(property, value)` (css-block.md §5.2's one rule, name-blind, total), typed values through `raw`'s §6 groundwork. What it buys: one hole spelling fewer (the `{ }` hole exists only because a value was a token span), the §4.1 lexer cost gone (no CSS value tokens — `100%`, `1rem`, `#333` never reach the lexer; the css block's `#333` refusal row retires), value-position completion becomes ordinary expression completion (the paper's Q4 half-dissolves: `pct(`, `Color::` complete as expressions), the formatter's value pass (§8) becomes expression formatting. BREAKING: 138 blocks — docs 14, corpus 4, vilan-core tests 80, vilan-cli tests 12, kolt 28 (at the owner's word); the codemod rides E167's converter machinery (it already types declarations)
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'change css block `property: value` into `property(value)` similar to the strategy taken for element syntax attributes'. OWNER QUESTIONS: (Q1) several arguments — `margin(px(4), px(8))` → `raw("margin", ..)` joined by single spaces (rec: yes, the typed `padding(a, b)` methods' own rule), or one argument only; (Q2) the codemod's value typing — bare CSS tokens become STRINGS (`overflow("hidden")`), `{expr}` holes become the expression, bare numbers stay numbers, and unit literals (`Npx`, `Nrem`, `N%`, `Nem`, `Nvh`, `Nvw`) become the prelude constructors (rec: yes — E167's converter already maps them; anything it cannot type stays a string); (Q3) custom properties `--name(value)` keep the leading dashes (rec: yes, as the hyphenated name rule)
items.body: Grammar (parsing.rs `parse_css_block` and friends; css-block.md §4.3 rewritten): `css-item = declaration | method-item | nested-rule`; `declaration = property "(" [ expression { "," expression } [ "," ] ] ")" ";"`; `property = { "-" } NAME { "-" NAME }` (span-adjacent, as today and as element attributes); `method-item = "." IDENT [ "(" args ")" ] ";"` → the method call on the chain; `nested-rule` unchanged (`.on(<set>) { … }`, `.pseudo(..) { … }`); the `value`/`value-piece`/`hole` productions DELETED. Desugar: unchanged target (`style()` chain; one `.raw(name, value)` per declaration; N arguments per Q1; a method item is the call). Rows: the `;` rule stays; the `#333` refusal row retires (no CSS tokens are lexed); a declaration argument whose type is not a raw value (`IntoRawValue` / the §6 set) is the ordinary type error at the argument. Tooling in the same order: formatter §8 (items print as calls; expression formatting inside), the TextMate css-block rules (property-call heads), `css_block_completions` (property position offers `name(` with the paren; value position falls through to expression completion), E167's converter both ways, E172/E175's StyleSurface unchanged. Codemod over the 138 blocks per Q2 (kolt's 28 at the owner's word, integrator at the sweep); CHANGELOG `breaking` entry with the three rewrites. Pins: each grammar production; the lowering identity (a block and its chain twin produce the same `class_list` and stylesheet — the existing css-block pins re-spelled); the converter round-trips; the formatter idempotent; docs: css-block.md §16 (the spelling change and why), the styling guide and reference. Sequence: after A95 S2 (Order 36) so the block head and the declaration form land on one surface.

items.title: NEW — completion at `css { .\| }` offers only the 14 std condition combinators (`css_block_completions`, vilan-ide completion.rs:718 — `CssPosition::Condition` → `STYLE_CONDITION_METHODS`): a CUSTOM `impl Style` method (kolt's `script_label` in theme.vl, `flex_row`, every app helper) and std's non-condition methods (`on`, `raw`) are absent, although the dotted head is exactly where an app writes them. Offer every `impl Style` method the file can reach: std's from the tables, the program's from its impl table (E172/E175's `StyleSurface` is the same source — reuse it), filtered by the B318 visibility bit under the uncurated-module exemption; with A101 the bare `.method();` items complete the same way
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'include custom impl methods in autocomplete at `css { .\| }`'. The vocabulary comes from the ANALYSIS (the impl table), not from a table — the position still comes from E67's raw re-parse
items.body: vilan-ide completion.rs: `CssPosition::Condition` (rename: `DottedHead`) merges `STYLE_CONDITION_METHODS`, std's other `impl Style` methods (from the program), and the program's user `impl Style` blocks (same file and sibling files — `StyleSurface::extend` after E175 feeds from the impl table); each entry carries the method's signature as detail and a `(` snippet; a nested-rule entry (`on`, `pseudo`, …) inserts `() { }` and a plain method inserts `();` once A101 lands (before A101: the block form only). Visibility: an unexported method of a curated module is filtered (B318 S1's bit; the uncurated exemption keeps everything). Pins: a user method in the same file; one in a sibling file; std's `on`; the combinators still first; the filtered case; the playground (vilan-wasm) reaches it unchanged.
